collection: NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics binary operations and open sentences
note: Original classroom practice. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Explain successive carries when adding binary numerals.
questions.prompt: A pupil adds 111 and 11, both in base two, and gives 110 as the result. Show the correct sum and explain what happens in the twos column.
questions.answer: 1010 in base two. The twos column contains three twos after the carry, so write 1 and carry 1 to the fours column.
questions.explanation: The ones column gives a carry. In the twos column, two of the three twos make a four and one two remains. The fours column then has two fours, making one eight.

markingGuide.description: Explains that the twos column contains three twos.
Writes 1 in that column and carries 1 four.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Recognise when a binary addition requires no carry.
questions.prompt: In base two, which pair can be added with no carry in any column?
questions.explanation: The first number uses the fours and ones places. The second uses the twos place only, so no column contains two 1s.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Regroup across a zero in binary subtraction.
questions.prompt: Use binary place values to subtract 11 from 100, with both numerals in base two. Show how the fours place supplies a one for the subtraction.
questions.answer: 1 in base two. Exchange one four for two twos, then exchange one of those twos for two ones.
questions.explanation: After both exchanges, 100 is represented by one two and two ones. Removing one two and one one leaves one one.

markingGuide.description: Exchanges one four for two twos.
Exchanges one two for two ones.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Subtracting by comparison with an addition
questions.learningObjective: Check a proposed binary difference using the inverse operation.
questions.prompt: A board shows 110 − 10 = 101, all in base two. Use addition to show why the displayed difference is wrong and to verify the correct difference.
questions.answer: The difference is 100. In base two, 101 + 10 = 111, whereas 100 + 10 = 110.
questions.explanation: Adding the amount removed to the proposed difference must recover the starting numeral. Only the corrected difference does so.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.
Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a binary multiplier shifts a partial product.
questions.prompt: A pupil multiplies 110 by 101 in base two. The multiplier has a 1 in the fours place. What partial product comes from that digit, before adding the other rows?
questions.explanation: The digit represents four groups of 110. Multiplying by four shifts the binary digits two places left and fills the ones and twos places with zeros.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Use binary place values to partition a multiplier and combine partial products.
questions.prompt: Find the product of 11 and 111 in base two. Split 111 into its fours, twos and ones, and give your result in base two.
questions.answer: 10101 in base two. The partial products are 1100, 110 and 11.
questions.explanation: The three rows represent 12, 6 and 3 in decimal. Their sum is 21, or 16 + 4 + 1, which is 10101 in base two.

markingGuide.description: Splits the multiplier into four, two and one.
Adds them to give 10101 in base two.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.
Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Identify a statement whose truth depends on the number substituted.
questions.prompt: Which line is an open number sentence that can become true or false when a number is put in the box?
questions.explanation: The equality is true when the box contains 11 and false for other numbers.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Test candidate numbers against an open sentence.
questions.prompt: A game card says 42 = □ + □. Both boxes stand for the same whole number. Ada chooses 20, Bala chooses 21 and Ngozi chooses 22. Who makes the equality true? Show the check.
questions.explanation: Each box must contain 21 because two equal addends make the total.

markingGuide.description: Substitutes 21 into both boxes and verifies the total.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Use the relationship between addition and subtraction to find the number removed.
questions.prompt: A number sentence reads 36 − n = 14. Write an addition sentence with the same three quantities and use it to find n.
questions.explanation: The amount remaining plus the amount taken away equals the starting amount.

markingGuide.description: Writes 14 + n = 36 or an equivalent addition.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Use multiplication to find an unknown dividend from its quotient and divisor.
questions.prompt: A label reads □ ÷ 7 = 12. Which calculation finds the missing number?
questions.explanation: The missing total consists of seven equal groups of 12. Their product is 84.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Represent two distinct shapes with letters and preserve repeated occurrences.
questions.prompt: In the sentence triangle + circle + triangle = 28, use t for triangle and c for circle. Write the sentence using letters. Explain what the two occurrences of t tell you.
questions.answer: t + c + t = 28, or 2t + c = 28. Both occurrences of t represent the same value.
questions.explanation: A single letter replaces every occurrence of its assigned shape, so the two triangles contribute t twice.

markingGuide.description: Uses t in both triangle positions and c in the circle position, or writes the equivalent simplified form.
Explains that both t terms refer to the same value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Solve a two-operation open sentence and check the result by substitution.
questions.prompt: Solve 5 + x/3 = 14. Show which operation you undo first and check your solution.
questions.answer: x = 27. Subtract 5 first, then multiply by 3. The check is 5 + 27/3 = 14.
questions.explanation: Removing 5 leaves x/3 = 9. Multiplying both sides by 3 isolates x.

markingGuide.description: Checks the solution in the original sentence.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Building an equation from a transaction
questions.learningObjective: Translate a purchase with a fixed extra cost into an open sentence.
questions.prompt: A club buys four matching folders and pays ₦350 to have all of them delivered. The total is ₦2,150. Use p for the price of one folder. Write and solve an equation for p.
questions.explanation: Subtract delivery once to get ₦1,800 for the four folders. Dividing by four gives ₦450 each.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Use a shared unknown on both sides to reason about an equality.
questions.prompt: Two trays balance. One holds three identical covered cups and six loose counters. The other holds one of the same cups and 22 loose counters. Each cup contains the same number of counters. Find that number and explain what remains after removing one cup from each tray.
questions.answer: 8 counters per cup. Removing one cup from each tray leaves two cups and six loose counters balancing 22 loose counters.
questions.explanation: With c counters per cup, 3c + 6 = c + 22. Removing one cup and then six loose counters from each side leaves 2c = 16.

markingGuide.description: Explains the equal removal and obtains 2c = 16.

verification.purpose: Verify the result in decimal notation.
